newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall sharply amid clashes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall sharply amid clashes.

text.p: Israeli shares fell sharply across the board in the wake of two days of bloody clashes between Palestinian and Israeli forces, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 4.04 percent, or 7.95 points, to 188.62 on a high all-share turnover of 147 million shekels against 82 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 index dropped 4.28 percent to 197.48.

"The market looks very bad and it fell beyond expectations. We saw panic in the market but despite that foreign investors were not selling. They are waiting to see how this will end," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.

"The main question is, are things still under control? If the whole situation gets out of control everything is possible. If it is still under control the events may give the peace process a real push," Nahum said.
In two days of bloody clashes between 33 Palestinians and 10 Israelis have been killed.
"We saw a very strong reaction to the events today. The whole market was falling. Investors are waiting now to see how events develop," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
"The future of the market depends now on the future of the peace process. It was interesting to see that foreign investors were using the opportunity to buy shares," he added.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 3.5 percent to 139,532 on high volume of 15.7 million shekels; Bezeq Israel Telecom, which plunged 5.5 percent to 793 on volume of 15.6 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which fell 3.0 percent to 28,548 on turnover of 6.0 million shekels.
